metadata.notes: Path D — Credential Access to Agent Interface. Scenario: LegitimateAgentCompromised (Layer 2 AI-Specific). Stolen credentials grant access to the agent's interface. Every subsequent agent action is pure #1 — legitimate functions being abused via a stolen identity. Notation: #4→[instant]#1→[instant]#1 + [DRE: C]. Velocity: VC-4 — after credential use, entire chain is machine-speed. MFA on agent interface creates a human-speed gate at step 1. Source: 'Agentic AI Under the Microscope — Why AI Security Is Not a Threat Category' (Bernhard Kreinz, 2026-02-25).

path_sequence.notes: Attacker uses stolen credentials to authenticate to agent interface. Generic vulnerability: insufficient identity-artifact binding at point of use (application phase per R-CRED). Credential acquisition is a separate prior step mapped to its enabling cluster. This step is the USE of the credential → always #4.
Attacker issues instructions to agent via authenticated session. Generic vulnerability: scope and trust in agent's instruction-processing capability.
Agent executes tool calls per attacker instructions. Generic vulnerability: scope and trust in agent's designed tool-use functions.
